extracted.intended_audience: scholars and practitioners in public relations, political communication, and crisis communication; social media researchers coding political tweets
extracted.subtask_description: Content-coding and measuring crisis communication strategies in politicians' Twitter posts (Trump and Cuomo) during COVID-19, using SCCT as a framework and inductively adding categories. Includes manifest metrics (retweets/favorites) and latent strategy codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit of analysis is the individual tweet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each tweet is coded separately. Coding decisions apply at the tweet level (not at user- or campaign-level).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tweet selection keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords used to identify COVID-19 related tweets: 'coronavirus', 'virus', 'pandemic', 'crisis', 'COVID 19', 'COVID-19'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After automated keyword filtering, a manual review process ensured tweets were actually related to COVID-19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion criteria for tweet sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Three exclusion criteria: (1) Unoriginal tweets, (2) Duplicated tweets, and (3) Tweets that did not show any crisis communication strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these exclusions during sample construction to retain only original, unique tweets that contain at least one crisis communication strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding scheme: dichotomous presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables were coded dichotomously (1 = presence of the category in the tweet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories are not mutually exclusive; a single tweet may receive multiple '1' codes across categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intercoder reliability procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Two researchers pre-coded 10% of the sample (n = 48) proportionate to tweet counts and calculated Krippendorff's alpha for intercoder reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After two rounds of revisions and reconciliations, Krippendorff's alpha ranged from .73–1 with an average of .94. Once acceptable reliability achieved, coders coded independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manifest content category: account
rubrics_metrics.description: Account indicates the tweet author (Trump or Cuomo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded for attribution/comparison across politicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manifest content category: date
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of the tweet, ranging in the study from January 24 to July 8, 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to situate tweets temporally and examine phases of crisis messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manifest content category: retweet count
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of retweets recorded at time of collection (Trump retweets from The Trump Archive; Cuomo retweets from exportcomments.com).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a measure of audience engagement; adjusted into engagement ratios to account for follower differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manifest content category: favorite (like) count
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of favorites/likes recorded at time of collection (source-specific).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside retweets to measure engagement; adjusted into engagement ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement ratio (retweet and favorite ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means of interactions per tweet per 1,000 followers (used to control for differences in follower counts between accounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate retweet_ratio = (mean retweets per tweet / follower_count) * 1000 (and similarly for favorites) following Lou et al., 2019 and TrackMaven, 2016.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent content category: DENY (collapsed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collapsed deny strategy: attempts to shift responsibility to other stakeholders (media, opposing party, administration, other races).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a collapsed nominal variable indicating presence of any deny subcategory in a tweet.

rubrics_metrics.name: DENY1: MEDIA
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = accusing media organizations of fake news, opposing reportage and stoking panic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Krippendorff's alpha reported as 1. Use this code when the tweet explicitly attacks or delegitimizes media coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: DENY2: DEMOCRATS/REPUBLICANS
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = criticizing Democrats in Trump’s case and Republicans in Cuomo’s case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 0.90. Code attacks framed at the opposing party as shifting blame or responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: DENY3: FEDERAL
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = criticizing Trump, his administration and the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 0.73. Use when a tweet blames federal actors/structures for problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: DENY4: EXCLUSION
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = projecting racial discriminations and xenophobia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 0.88. Code tweets that otherize, scapegoat, or stigmatize racial/ethnic groups or foreigners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent content category: DIMINISH
rubrics_metrics.description: Diminish strategy: downplaying the fatalness of the virus and the likelihood of contagion; describing the U.S. situation in a non-severe manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 1 (for DIMINISH variable in Table 1). Code when tweet minimizes severity or risk of COVID-19 (e.g., likening to seasonal flu).

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent content category: BOLSTERING (collapsed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collapsed bolstering strategy: expressions of appreciation for government, action praise, emotional support, and information transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a collapsed indicator if any bolstering subcategory appears in a tweet; analysis showed bolstering often negatively correlated with retweet ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOLSTERING1: GOVERNMENT (government praise)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = mentioning Trump/Cuomo’s achievements as leaders; mentioning the achievements of the government (Trump) or local government (Cuomo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 0.91. Code praise of leadership/administration accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOLSTERING2: ACTIONS (action praise)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = ingratiating the proactive measures in handling the virus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 1. Code tweets praising specific actions/policies taken to address the crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOLSTERING3: EMOTIONAL SUPPORT
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = conveying empathy; building intimacy; delivering encouragement, assurance and confidence; using emotional appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 0.91. Code expressions of compassion, support, and reassurance to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOLSTERING4: TRANSPARENCY (information transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = praising and promoting transparency in information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 0.90. Code when tweets emphasize clear/transparent information sharing or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent content category: COHESION (collapsed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohesion: intentions to promote cooperation, cohesion, and inclusion among various social members, institutions, and groups (new category not in original SCCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collapsed indicator capturing any cohesion subcategory; emerged inductively from tweets and grouped separately from SCCT's four standard strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: COHESION1: PARTISANSHIP
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = creating party cooperation to tackle the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 1. Code appeals to cross-party or party unity actions to address the crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: COHESION2: INSTITUTIONAL COOPERATION
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = promoting institutional cooperation, including cooperation with the federal government and different state governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 1. Code tweets calling for intergovernmental or inter-institutional collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: COHESION3: RALLY-ROUND-THE-FLAG (patriotism)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = eliciting patriotism, societal cohesion and loyalty to the country/states to tackle the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 1. Code appeals to national unity, patriotism, or collective identity to address crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: COHESION4: INCLUSION (social inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = criticizing those who discriminated minorities; promoting integration and cooperation among different ethnic and social groups; and enhancing benefits for vulnerable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alpha = 1. Code explicit promotion of inclusion or criticism of discriminatory behavior; in study, Cuomo used this more than Trump.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping to SCCT categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison and mapping of observed categories to Coombs' Situational Crisis Communication Theory (SCCT) four response strategies (deny, diminish, bolstering, rebuild) and identification of a new 'cohesion' category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SCCT's definitions as a baseline: informing/adjusting recommended for victim cluster; rebuild includes apology/compensation (not observed here). The coder should map subcategories to SCCT when applicable and create new categories when inductively observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding notes on category overlap and analysis waves
rubrics_metrics.description: Two waves of analysis: (1) collapse subcategories into four nominal collapsed strategies to indicate presence of any sub-strategy; (2) examine presence of each individual theme as proportions of tweet population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For statistical tests, both collapsed and individual-category coding frames were used (chi-square/Fisher's exact tests, correlations with engagement ratios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Codebook availability and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed codebook containing instructions and examples is provided (Appendix A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the codebook for example tweets, inclusion/exclusion rules per code, and edge-case guidance during coding.
